# `m.indicators.macd`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

The moving average convergence/divergence of a ticker's bars, one row per bar.

```python
m.indicators.macd(symbols, *, short_window=12, long_window=26, signal_window=9, timespan=dm.Timespan.DAY, series_type=dm.SeriesType.CLOSE, adjusted=True, start=None, end=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None)
```

[All datasets](README.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Verbs | `fetch()`, `poll()` |
| Served by | REST |
| Time range | `start` and `end` are sent as `timestamp.gte` and `timestamp.lt` |
| `poll()` | `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`: holds exactly the latest cycle's rows, keyed by `Symbol` and `TimestampStart` |
| `filters` | none |

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | Tickers of any asset class. | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and each one you delete stops being read. `last_by()`, `fetch()`, `history()`, and most polls also drop a deleted symbol's rows. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; by default, a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |
| `short_window` | The bars of the fast exponential average. |  |
| `long_window` | The bars of the slow exponential average. |  |
| `signal_window` | The bars of the signal line's average. |  |
| `timespan` | The bar size, `MINUTE` or longer. | The unit of each bar, a `dm.Timespan` member: `SECOND`, `MINUTE`, `HOUR`, `DAY`, `WEEK`, `MONTH`, `QUARTER`, or `YEAR`; futures take `SESSION` in place of `DAY`. Text such as `"day"` raises `TypeError`: write `dm.Timespan.DAY`, or convert text with `dm.Timespan("day")`. One-second and one-minute bars with `multiplier=1` also stream; every other length is history only. |
| `series_type` | The bar price the indicator is computed from. |  |
| `adjusted` | Split-adjusted bars. Crypto has no adjusted bars, so `False` fails the read of a crypto symbol. | `True`, the default, gives split-adjusted prices, restated in terms of every later stock split; `False` gives prices as traded. Only REST adjusts: flat files and live bars are always as traded. |
| `start` | The first bar's start. | The first day or moment of the range. A date (text such as `"2025-06-02"`, a Python `date`, or a Deephaven `LocalDate`) means the day in the market's time zone: New York for stocks, options, and indices; UTC for forex and crypto; for futures, the trading session that ends that day. An instant is an exact time: a Python `datetime` with a time zone, a `pandas.Timestamp`, a `numpy.datetime64`, a Deephaven `Instant` or `ZonedDateTime`, or Deephaven time text such as `"2025-06-02T09:30 ET"`. Give `start` and `end` as two dates or two instants. A `datetime` without a time zone raises `ValueError`, and a calendar-date field, such as an ex-dividend date, takes dates only. |
| `end` | The end of the range, of the same kind as `start`. | The last day, or the moment the range stops, in the same form as `start`. A date includes its whole day, so `start="2025-06-02", end="2025-06-02"` reads all of June 2; an instant is excluded. Leave it out to read through now; a list dataset then sends Massive no end, so it also returns records still to come, such as dividends announced but not yet paid. |
| `order` | The direction of the bars' times. The endpoints have no `sort`. | The direction of `sort`: `dm.Order.ASC` or `dm.Order.DESC`. |
| `limit` | The most rows for each symbol. | The most rows Massive returns for the whole request, across every symbol you name, kept in Massive's order: ask for newest first (`order=dm.Order.DESC`) to keep the latest. A symbol that comes first can use up the whole limit, so leave `limit` out when you need every row of each symbol. A `fetch()` that follows a table of symbols applies it to each symbol's request, and this dataset's own line says where else it applies to each symbol. |
| `filters` | Further endpoint parameters. | Any other parameter Massive documents for this dataset, as a mapping from the parameter's name to its value, with each dot in the name written as `_`: Massive's `strike_price.gte` is `strike_price_gte`. This page lists the keys the dataset takes. A key it doesn't take, or one that has its own argument, such as `start`, raises `ValueError` naming the keys it does take. A date or time value takes ISO 8601 text, or any value `start` takes. |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST `/v1/indicators/macd/{stockTicker}`: the request's `stockTicker` parameter; REST `/v1/indicators/macd/{cryptoTicker}`: the request's `cryptoTicker` parameter. | REST |
| `Date` | String | The trading day of the bar, as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: the date of `TimestampStart` in the day zone of the symbol's class (UTC for forex and crypto, New York otherwise) for an intraday or 1-day bar, and null for a bar that spans more than one date (several days, a week or longer, or an intraday bar that crosses midnight). Joining an intraday row to the same day's daily bar on `Date` attaches values not known until that day ended, and a null `Date` matches another null, so join longer bars on `TimestampEnd`. | REST |
| `TimestampStart` | Instant | The start of the bar the value is computed at, as an Instant. A bar of a day or longer starts at 00:00 of its window's first day in the day zone of the symbol's class (UTC for forex and crypto, New York otherwise). A bar of a day or longer stamped at a time or on a day Massive is not known to use keeps that stamp, has a null `Date`, and ends one period after it, with a WARNING, since which day it covers is not known. From REST `timestamp`: "The Unix Msec timestamp from the last aggregate used in this calculation." | REST |
| `TimestampEnd` | Instant | The exclusive end of the bar's window, as an Instant: the first instant at which the bar is complete, so an as-of join on it, `t.aj(bars, on=["Symbol", "Timestamp>=TimestampEnd"])`, never attaches a bar that is still open. It is when the window closes, not when Massive published the bar, and Massive may correct a bar later. An intraday bar ends its length after its start; a bar of a day or longer at 00:00, in the day zone of the symbol's class, after its window's last day. A row read before its window ended has `TimestampInsert` before `TimestampEnd`, and its values can still change; `t.where("TimestampEnd <= TimestampInsert")` keeps only the rows read after their window ended. That test reads the local clock, which can be off, and a row read within moments of its end, or from a delayed feed, may still lack the window's last trades; an end set later than the window's (an index day's extra hour, a stamp kept as sent) only keeps a finished row out longer. | REST |
| `Value` | double | The MACD line value, calculated as the difference between the short-term and long-term exponential moving averages (EMAs) based on the periods specified in the request parameters. | REST |
| `Histogram` | double | The difference between the MACD line (value) and the signal line (signal). Positive histogram values indicate upward (bullish) momentum, while negative histogram values indicate downward (bearish) momentum. | REST |
| `Signal` | double | The signal line value, calculated as the exponential moving average (EMA) of the MACD line (value) over the signal period defined in the request parameters. Traders typically use crossovers between the MACD and signal lines as trading signals. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
